name: Dropbox
tagline: Create a scoped Dropbox app and plug it into Composio. Works for you at once; past 50 linked users you need production approval.

approvalWait.asStated: "We respond to nearly all production requests within a few business days." Review starts only once the app has linked 50 users.

cost.asStated: Is use of the Dropbox API free? Yes! There's no cost to you as the developer.

steps.title: Set up your Composio account
steps.when: Skip if you already have a Composio project and API key.
instructions: Sign up from the Composio login page.
Open Settings → API keys and copy a key.
Save it as COMPOSIO_API_KEY where your agent runs.
Stay in this project. Auth configs belong to one project.

problems.q: I can't find the API keys page
a: Open the API keys link above after signing in. It opens Settings → API keys for your current project.
If you have several projects, switch to the one you'll use for this agent first.

steps.title: Create a Dropbox app
instructions: Open the App Console and click Create app.
Choose an API: Scoped access.
Choose the access type. App folder: only /Apps/<your app>. Full Dropbox: every file. Pick the least your tools need.
Name the app, then click Create app. Users see the name when they connect.
Don't use "Dropbox", start with "drop", or use DBX or DB in the name. Production review rejects it.

warnings.text: The access type is permanent. Switching from App folder to Full Dropbox means deleting the app and creating a new one.
Dropbox requires developers on platforms like Composio to use their own app key. That's what this guide sets up.

problems.q: I picked App folder but my tools need other folders
a: The access type can't be changed. Delete the app under Settings and create a new one with Full Dropbox.
You'll get a new App key and secret. Update your Composio auth config.

steps.title: Add the redirect URI
instructions: On the Settings tab, scroll to OAuth 2 → Redirect URIs.
Paste the URI below and click Add.
Turn off Allow implicit grant. Composio uses the code flow.

fields.label: Redirect URI
fields.hint: Must match the Redirect URI in your Composio auth config exactly

warnings.text: Composio's Dropbox auth config may prefill an older /api/v1/auth-apps/add URI. Set the v3 callback in both places.

steps.unconfirmed: We couldn't sign in to check the implicit grant control's exact labels.

problems.q: Dropbox rejects the redirect URI when a user connects
a: Dropbox only redirects to URIs listed under Redirect URIs, matched exactly.
Paste the same v3 callback in Dropbox and in your Composio auth config.

steps.title: Choose scopes
instructions: Open the Permissions tab.
Tick the scopes below. account_info.read is already on and required.
Add sharing.read or sharing.write only if your tools share files or folders.
Click Submit at the bottom of the page. Changes aren't saved until you do.
These scopes are the most Composio can ask for. Every scope in your auth config must be ticked here.

fields.label: Starter scopes
fields.hint: Drop the .write scopes for read-only tools

warnings.text: Changing scopes later doesn't update users who already connected. They must reconnect to get the new scopes.
Production review checks you don't ask for broader access than your app uses.

steps.unconfirmed: Dropbox's docs don't mention the Submit button. We took it from Dropbox forum reports and couldn't sign in to see it.

a: Scroll to the bottom of the Permissions tab and click Submit.

problems.q: A tool fails with 401 after I added a scope
a: The user's grant still has the old scopes. Dropbox never adds scopes to existing grants.
Have the user reconnect.

steps.title: Copy the App key and secret
instructions: On the Settings tab, copy the App key. That's your client ID.
Reveal the App secret and copy it. That's your client secret.
Store the secret in a secret manager, never in git.
steps.unconfirmed: We couldn't sign in to see how the App Console reveals the App secret.

a: The App key or secret in Composio is wrong, or they come from different apps.
Copy both again from the same app's Settings tab.

steps.title: Create a Composio auth config
instructions: Open the Dropbox toolkit in Composio and create an auth config.
Choose OAuth2 and turn on your own developer credentials.
Paste the App key as Client ID and the App secret as Client secret.
Replace the default scopes with yours. The default list includes openid, contacts and file requests scopes.
Save, then copy the auth config ID (ac_…) for the next step.

fields.label: Redirect URI
fields.hint: Overwrite the prefilled v1 URL if one appears

fields.label: Scopes
fields.hint: Comma separated. Same scopes as the Permissions tab

warnings.text: Background access needs token_access_type=offline. Without it Dropbox gives no refresh token and short-lived tokens just expire.
warnings.unconfirmed: We couldn't see whether Composio sends token_access_type=offline. Check the connection still works a few hours later.

steps.unconfirmed: The link exists. We couldn't check, without logging in, whether it opens auth config creation directly. If not: Auth Configs → Create Auth Config.

problems.q: The link didn't open the Dropbox toolkit
a: Open Auth Configs in the Composio dashboard and click Create Auth Config.
Pick Dropbox, choose OAuth2, and turn on your own developer credentials.

steps.title: Use the auth config in your agent
instructions: Pass the auth config ID when you create a session. Your coding agent can paste this in.
Toolkits you don't list keep using Composio's managed auth.

a: The session must include authConfigs with your ac_… ID for dropbox.
Toolkits not listed in authConfigs fall back to managed auth.

steps.title: Connect a test account
instructions: Start a connection for a test user and open the link.
Sign in with your own Dropbox account. A new app only links to its owner.
The consent screen should show your app name and the scopes you picked.
Dropbox checks the App key before sign-in. A typo shows an error page straight away.
Users already connected through managed auth must reconnect.
steps.unconfirmed: We didn't run a full connection. It needs a Composio API key and a real Dropbox sign-in.

problems.q: Dropbox shows an error page instead of sign-in
a: Dropbox doesn't recognise the App key (unknown_client_id).
Copy the App key again from the app's Settings tab into your Composio auth config.
The token is invalid, expired, or the user unlinked your app in Dropbox. Retrying won't help.
Have the user reconnect.

problems.q: The consent screen still says Composio
a: The connection used the managed auth config. Pass your ac_… ID in the session.
Existing connections keep their old config. Delete and reconnect them.

steps.title: Let other users connect
instructions: On the Settings tab, under Development users, click Enable additional users.
Your app can now link up to 500 Dropbox users while in development.
At 50 linked users a two-week clock starts. Apply for production before then.

warnings.text: Miss the two weeks after 50 users and new links freeze until you're approved. Unlinking users doesn't unfreeze it.

problems.q: Other people can't connect, but I can
a: New apps only link to their owner. Click Enable additional users under Development users.

problems.q: New users can't link any more
a: Your app passed 50 users and two weeks without production approval, so Dropbox froze new links.
The only fix is to apply for and get production status.

steps.title: Apply for production
steps.when: Before your app passes 50 linked users. Internal tools and demos can stay in development.
instructions: Fill in the Branding tab: publisher, description, app website and icons. Users see these on the consent screen.
Have a privacy policy specific to your app.
Fix the name first. Once in production only Dropbox support can rename it.
On the Settings tab, under Status, click Apply for Production.
Describe how you use the API and upload your icon. More detail can speed approval.
Need review before 50 users? Explain why under Request early review.

warnings.text: Your logo can't include or resemble a Dropbox logo or the word Dropbox.

a: Dropbox sends feedback. Fix the issues and resubmit from the Settings tab.
Common causes: a name or logo against the branding guide, or broader access than your app uses.

problems.q: I need to rename my app after approval
a: You can't rename it yourself. Open an API support ticket and Dropbox can do it.

steps.title: Wait for production approval
instructions: Dropbox reviews your request only once your app has linked 50 users, unless you asked for early review.
After approval any number of users can link.

wait.asStated: "We respond to nearly all production requests within a few business days." Review starts only once the app has linked 50 users.
